title:
From raw footage
to a reviewed edit
subtitle: Codex Media Studio • Quick-start tutorial
steps: Follow one example: edit a short desk-setup video.
Text-led walkthrough • pause whenever you need.
cards: Use desktop Codex while sign-in is unresolved.
Give precise feedback on each revision.
tip: Illustrated workflow — not a screen recording.

title: 01  Create a production
subtitle: Keep one project folder for one video.
steps: Choose New. Name the folder “Desk setup”.
Choose Import footage or documents, or drop your files.
Wait for import to finish; check the listed sources.
cards: Studio copies files into the production.
tip: Example filenames are illustrative. Originals stay intact.

title: 02  Give the edit a purpose
subtitle: A useful brief describes the result, not just “make it better”.
steps: Fill in audience, takeaway, length and tone.
Use Keep or emphasize for details that must survive.
Add editing context, then choose Save brief.
cards: Beginners • a clearer, more comfortable desk
Keep the warning. Use the corrected second take.
tip: Save before switching tabs. Refresh does not save draft text.

title: 03  Explain your references
subtitle: A link needs a role and a reason.
steps: Enter a descriptive Label and the resource URL.
Choose Source, Reference or Background; select Add link.
Explain which part matters in your brief.
cards: Material that belongs in this edit
An example of the pace or look you want
Context that helps the editor understand
tip: Adding a link records it; it does not download or analyze it.

title: 04  Choose your resources
subtitle: Selections are preferences, not setup or permission.
steps: Keep local tools for transcription, cleanup and rendering.
Choose Remotion when the edit needs motion graphics.
Ask Codex to check readiness before generation.
cards: Native Codex images need scoped approval.
tip: Run one heavy local model at a time. A selection installs nothing.

title: 05  Continue in desktop Codex
subtitle: Use this route while Studio sign-in remains unresolved.
steps: Save your brief, resource choices and feedback.
Choose Export handoff; its text is copied for you.
Paste it into desktop Codex and add the example request.
cards: Read this handoff and inspect my sources.
Document source understanding and an edit strategy.
Make a short representative preview, then register it as a revision.
tip: Export handoff sends context, not a video. Use subscription Codex.

title: 06  Understand before cutting
subtitle: The editor should explain the source and the proposed changes.
steps: Read the source understanding and edit strategy.
Check that the argument, warning and conclusion survive.
Ask Codex to record actual evidence for each stage.
cards: What is here, and what does it mean?
Are the actual delivery files ready?
tip: Evidence records real work. It does not make an unfinished check pass.

title: 07  Review a real revision
subtitle: A completed render is the start of review.
steps: Choose Refresh after Codex registers the preview.
Select the output in Viewing, then play it with sound.
Use Add revision if you need to register an output yourself.
cards: Source or a specific output revision
Meaning • timing • readable graphics • clear speech
Select versions one at a time.
tip: Review the rendered file, not only a transcript or still image.

title: 08  Leave precise feedback
subtitle: Point to the problem and describe the intended result.
steps: Seek to the issue; choose Pause & annotate.
Optionally draw a region or enter a range end in seconds.
Write what should change and why; choose Save annotation.
cards: The label covers the cable connection.
Move it above the desk; keep the connection visible.
The captured frame and time stay with this revision.
tip: Capture first. A rectangle alone does not save a comment.

title: 09  Check the correction
subtitle: Feedback acceptance is your decision.
steps: Export a fresh handoff and ask Codex for the correction.
Play the replacement revision and inspect the change.
On the original note, choose its Replacement revision and add Resolution notes.
cards: It is waiting for your inspection.
Accept only after review, or explain what still needs work.
tip: Each status change needs notes. Codex must not accept for you.

title: 10  Export after quality review
subtitle: Technical checks and creative acceptance are separate.
steps: Ask desktop Codex to validate the final file and record QA.
Watch the whole export at normal speed with audio.
Keep unresolved findings visible and request fixes.
cards: Save the final MP4. Publication is a separate decision.
tip: Nothing in this walkthrough authorizes an upload.

title: Keep the guide beside you
subtitle: Start with a small preview. Improve one revision at a time.
steps: Choose How to Use and search for a task or control.
Use Help for this tab to keep your current draft underneath.
Copy an example, adapt it, and paste it into Codex.
cards: Retained or deferred does not mean ready to run.
Import your own footage and write a meaningful brief.
tip: This film explains the workflow; it does not qualify raw-footage editing.
